conflict_title: Side Wall Bounces vs Table Out-of-Bounds
arcade_pong_behavior: Side walls are active boundary cushions. When the ball collides with the left or right wall, it reflects elastically with angle-preserving velocity and remains live in the rally.
table_tennis_regulation: Under ITTF 2026 Statute §2.7.1, there are no side walls. Any ball that touches any fixture, ceiling, wall, or floor outside the playing table immediately terminates the rally with a point awarded to the opponent.
system_resolution: When match profile is ARCADE_PONG, wall ricochets are legal game mechanics. When match profile is TABLE_TENNIS_TRAINING, any wall collision is counted as an out-of-bounds fault and terminates the rally.

arcade_pong_behavior: Arcade Pong has no vertical net mesh; the arena is a flat bounding box where the ball traverses directly from player end to opponent end.
table_tennis_regulation: Under ITTF 2026 Statute §2.2.1 and §2.7.1, a physical net of 15.25cm height divides the courts. A ball touching the net on service is a Let (§2.9.1), and during a rally must clear or graze the net assembly to land in the opposing court.
system_resolution: In TABLE_TENNIS_TRAINING mode, net trajectories are simulated and trajectory faults trigger Let or Point calls according to ITTF §2.9.1.

conflict_title: Target Score: 11 Points Margin of 2 vs First to N
arcade_pong_behavior: Arcade Pong matches default to first-to-11 or first-to-21 without requiring a two-point margin deuce rule unless specifically configured in arcade options.
table_tennis_regulation: Under ITTF 2026 Statute §2.11.1, a game is won by the first player reaching 11 points, except at 10-10 where a 2-point lead is strictly mandatory.
system_resolution: TABLE_TENNIS_TRAINING enforces strict deuce win-by-two logic and best-of-5/7 match progression under ITTF §2.11.1 and §2.12.1.

conflict_title: Direct Volley Serve vs Double Bounce Service
arcade_pong_behavior: In Arcade Pong, the ball resets to center or paddle origin and is served directly toward the opponent without requiring a table-side bounce.
table_tennis_regulation: Under ITTF 2026 Statute §2.6.3, the ball must bounce on the server's half of the table before crossing the net and bouncing on the receiver's court.
system_resolution: TABLE_TENNIS_TRAINING tracks bounce events and flags direct hits on service as illegal service faults.
